exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Taipei Control, Cathay two five one, level Flight Level three tree zero.
exchanges.meaning: Reports cruising at Flight Level 330 on initial contact with Taipei Control.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Taipei Control, caution severe mountain wave activity reported west of waypoint MEGAR, moderate to severe turbulence.
exchanges.meaning: Warns of severe mountain wave activity and moderate-to-severe turbulence west of waypoint MEGAR.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Caution mountain wave acknowledged, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Acknowledges the mountain wave caution to ATC.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Taipei Control, Cathay two five one, unable maintain Flight Level three tree zero due severe downdraft, descending through Flight Level three two five, request turn left heading zero fow-er zero to exit wave.
exchanges.meaning: Mandatory ICAO call: declares inability to maintain FL330 due severe downdraft and requests an oblique escape turn to exit the wave.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, roger, turn left heading zero fow-er zero approved, maintain Flight Level three wun zero or above, report level.
exchanges.meaning: Approves the escape turn, assigns a new minimum level of FL310 or above, and requests a level report.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Turn left heading zero fow-er zero, maintain Flight Level three wun zero or above, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Full readback of the approved escape turn and the new altitude constraint.

vocabulary.definition: Standing atmospheric gravity waves triggered by airflow over ridges.
Mandatory notification when downdraft exceeds climb performance; the emergency clearance deviation call.
Low-level turbulent vortices beneath wave crests; severe structural turbulence zone.
Pressure drop over ridges causing altimeters to over-read true height; can deceive pilots by 1,000+ ft.

quiz.question: When flying on the leeward side of a mountain ridge in strong winds, how does the localized pressure drop caused by the Venturi effect affect the barometric altimeter reading?
options: The altimeter indicates higher than the actual true altitude of the aircraft.
The altimeter indicates lower than the actual true altitude.
quiz.explanation: The Venturi acceleration of wind over ridges drops static pressure. Altimeters interpret lower pressure as higher altitude, causing the instrument to over-read true altitude.

quiz.question: What is the primary piloting technique if an aircraft encounters a severe mountain wave downdraft that exceeds climb performance?
options: Pull the yoke to full aft stop to maintain exact altitude.
Maintain pitch attitude for turbulence penetration speed (V_RA), set max continuous thrust, accept altitude loss within safe limits, and turn obliquely away from the ridge to exit the wave.
quiz.explanation: Pulling up to fight a 3,000 ft/min downdraft risks an aerodynamic stall. Pilots fly V_RA, set climb thrust, turn away from the mountain wave crest, and notify ATC.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body: Mountain wave activity: standing atmospheric gravity waves triggered by airflow over ridges ("Caution severe mountain wave activity"). Unable maintain FL due downdraft: mandatory notification when downdraft exceeds climb performance — emergency clearance deviation call. Rotor clouds / Roll clouds: low-level turbulent vortices beneath wave crests — severe structural turbulence zone. Venturi altimeter error: pressure drop over ridges causing altimeters to over-read true height; can deceive pilots by 1,000+ ft.

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body: Day 22 Review (+1d): PIREP structure: Aircraft type, location, time UTC, level, intensity. Fly turbulence penetration speed (V_RA). Day 10 Review (+14d): In cold weather, indicated altitude is higher than true altitude ("from warm to cold, look out below").

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact
sections.body: In Patagonia, the Airbus Perlan Mission II glider rode massive stratospheric mountain waves to reach 76,124 feet — higher than the cruising altitude of a U-2 spy plane — completely unpowered! Mountain waves also create stationary, lens-shaped Altocumulus Lenticularis clouds hovering above ridges, historically responsible for more UFO sightings than any other meteorological phenomenon!
